title: Day Market: a season of market days (wholesale buying with spoiling batches, a stall layout with prices, a walking-visitor simulation with tills and a queue, orders, rent, upgrades), three save slots, stamps, records, two languages
brief: Build a game called Day Market.
The game

- You keep a produce stall at a day market for a season of days. Each day has four parts, in order: the Morning (buy goods from the wholesaler, perhaps take an order), the Stall (lay out crates and set prices), the Day (the market runs by itself: visitors walk past the stall, take goods, queue at the till and pay) and the Evening (the order, spoilage, rent and stamps, then upgrades). A season is 7 days long, or 3 if the setting says so.
- Coins are whole numbers throughout. Every division is rounded down.
Data

- The goods, in catalogue order (wholesale base price, reference price, life in days): apples 2, 4, 5; bread 3, 6, 1; cheese 6, 11, 6; fish 7, 14, 2; flowers 3, 7, 2; honey 5, 9, never (honey never spoils).

- The visitor types (how many different goods it wants, units it takes of each, budget, the most it pays as a percentage of a good's reference price, patience in the queue in minutes, haggles): cook 2, 2, 40, 120, 15, no; tourist 1, 1, 20, 150, 6, no; bargain 2, 1, 20, 100, 20, yes; regular 3, 1, 30, 110, 10, no.

- The goods, the visitor types, the hourly visitor rates and the weather numbers (under Day), the upgrades (under Evening) and the stamps (under Stamps and records) are data kept apart from the code: changing one of these numbers is changing a file of data.
Season

- A new season starts on day 1 with coins 60 at Easy, 50 at Normal, 40 at Hard; reputation 50; no stock; an empty stall; every good priced at its reference price; no upgrades; no order. Its difficulty and its length are the settings when it starts, and stay the season's whatever the settings say later. Its seed is the `seed` the game was started with (default 1), kept with the season.

- When a season starts, the weather of each of its days is drawn from a random source seeded by the season's seed, each day on its own: sun 4 in 10, cloud 3 in 10, rain 2 in 10, heat 1 in 10. This list is the forecast.

- Every other draw of a day comes from a random source started afresh at the start of that day's Morning from the season's seed and the day's number (how they are combined is yours), in this order: the six wholesale prices (catalogue order); then, on day 2 and later, the order; then, when the day opens, the visitors. So a day's draws never depend on what happened on the days before it.
- Reputation is a whole number from 0 to 100 and never goes past either end.
Morning

- When a Morning starts, in order: the day's wholesale prices are drawn, each good's base plus a whole number from -1 to +2 (each equally likely); on day 2 and later an order is drawn: a good (each equally likely) and 4, 6 or 8 units (each equally likely), paying units times the good's reference price times 3 / 2 (rounded down); the day's taken, served, walked out, passed, spoiled, sales and visitors are cleared; and the season is saved in its slot as it stands at that moment.

- The Morning's rows are To the stall, then the six goods in catalogue order. Enter on To the stall opens the Stall. Enter on a good buys a lot of 6 units at the day's wholesale price (6 times the price in coins) when the coins are enough and the good's stock would not go past 99 units. With too few coins it changes nothing and the screen shows "Not enough coins" until the next word is given; past 99 units it changes nothing.

- Stock is kept in batches: a batch is a number of units of one good with the days it has left (honey's batches have none). A lot bought has the good's life as its days left; a good's batches with the same days left are one batch. Units leave stock from the good's batch with the fewest days left first.
- accept takes the day's order when there is one and it is not taken yet; otherwise it changes nothing. A taken order is settled in the Evening. Nothing keeps its units for it: visitors may buy them.
Stall

- The stall is a grid 6 cells wide and 2 deep. A cell is (x, y): x from 0 to 5 left to right, y 0 for the front row (by the aisle) and 1 for the back row. A cell is empty or holds one crate of one good. At most 8 crates (12 with Extra crates). The stall and the prices stay as they were left from day to day, and are part of the season.

- Each time the Stall opens the cursor is at (0, 0) and the selected good is apples. Up / Down / Left / Right move the cursor one cell (Up raises y) and stop at the edges. next_good moves the selection along the catalogue (apples, bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey, apples...), prev_good the other way round. put places a crate of the selected good on the cursor's cell when the cell is empty and the crates are below the limit; otherwise it changes nothing. take removes the crate on the cursor's cell; on an empty cell it changes nothing. price_up and price_down change the selected good's price by 1 coin, never below 1 or above 3 times its reference price; a price is the same for every crate of that good. Enter opens the day, whatever the stall holds (even nothing).
Day

- The day runs from 08:00 to 16:00: 480 minutes of game time, the clock. When the day opens the clock is 0, the speed is slow and minute 0 is played at once. Each time the clock goes up by one to c, minute c is played. When the clock reaches 480 the day is over and that minute is not played.

- Speed. The day keeps a progress number, 0 when it opens; every tick on the day screen adds 3 at slow, 12 at fast, 60 at rush and 0 at hold; whenever it reaches 60, 60 is taken off it and the clock goes up by one. A change of speed keeps what the progress holds. (So a minute is 20 ticks at slow, 5 at fast, 1 at rush.) The words hold, slow, fast and rush set the speed. finish plays every minute left, one after another as rush would, and the day is over, all before the next tick.

- Visitors. When the day opens, every minute from 0 to 479, in order, makes three draws whatever happens: a number r from 0 to 99; a type (cook 3 in 10, tourist 3 in 10, bargain 2 in 10, regular 2 in 10); and the type's wants (as many different goods as the type wants, drawn one at a time, each good not drawn yet equally likely, kept in the order drawn). A visitor arrives at that minute when r is below A = H times W times (50 + reputation) / 10000 (rounded down), where H is the hour's rate (10, 15, 20, 15, 12, 18, 15, 8 for the hours that start at 08:00, 09:00 ... 15:00), W is the weather's number (sun 100, cloud 90, rain 50, or 80 with Awning, heat 70) and reputation is as it stood when the day opened. At most one visitor arrives in a minute. Visitors are numbered 1, 2, 3... in order of arrival. This is the day's visitor list.

- The aisle runs in front of the stall: cells 0 to 5, in line with the stall's columns. A visitor arriving at minute m is at aisle cell 0 at minute m, cell 1 at m + 1, and so on to cell 5 at m + 5; at minute m + 6 it leaves the aisle.

- Looking. A visitor at aisle cell x looks at the stall's front cell (x, 0), then at the back cell (x, 1) if its basket already holds something (with Sign: always). At a crate it takes the crate's good when all of these hold: the good is on its wants and not in its basket yet; the price times 100 is at most the good's reference price times the type's percentage; the type's units times the price is at most its budget left; and the units available (the good's stock minus the units of that good in every visitor's basket, on the aisle, in the queue and at the tills) are at least the type's units. Taking puts the type's units into its basket at that price, and its budget left goes down by units times price.

- The tills. There is one till (two with Second till). A till serves one visitor at a time; a service that starts at minute s ends at minute s + 2 + the number of goods in the basket. When it ends the visitor pays the basket's total (a bargain visitor pays the total less a tenth of it, the tenth rounded down); the coins and the day's taken go up by what is paid; the units leave stock; served goes up by 1; reputation goes up by 1; and the sale is recorded.

- The queue. A visitor who leaves the aisle with something in its basket joins the end of the queue, and its joined minute is that minute; with nothing, it goes, and passed goes up by 1. A queued visitor's wait is the clock minus its joined minute. A queued visitor (not yet at a till) whose wait reaches its type's patience leaves: its goods go back (they are available again), reputation goes down by 2 and walked out goes up by 1.

- Each minute is played in this order: (1) every till whose service ends this minute finishes it; (2) every queued visitor whose wait has reached its patience leaves; (3) the visitors on the aisle, from the lowest number, each move one cell on, and one moving on from cell 5 leaves the aisle (to the queue, or gone); (4) the visitor arriving this minute, if any, enters at cell 0; (5) the visitors on the aisle, from the lowest number, look; (6) each free till, till 1 first, takes the visitor at the front of the queue.
- When the day is over, the visitors still on the aisle, in the queue or at a till are gone: they pay nothing and are counted neither as walked out nor as passed.

- A day's result (its coins, taken, served, walked out, passed, sales, and the evening after it) depends only on the season as the day opened and the day's draws, never on the speed the clock was run at.
Evening

- When the day is over, this happens at once, in order: (1) the facts for the stamps are taken; (2) a taken order: when the good's stock holds the order's units they leave stock and the coins go up by its pay (delivered); otherwise it fails and reputation goes down by 5; (3) spoilage: every batch's days left goes down by 1, or by 2 on a heat day without Cool box, and a batch at 0 or below is thrown away (its units are spoiled); honey never spoils; (4) rent: the coins go down by 15 at Easy, 20 at Normal or 30 at Hard (the season's difficulty), plus 2 for each crate on the stall; (5) stamps are earned; (6) when the coins are below 0 the season ends bankrupt, with score 0; otherwise, on the season's last day, the season ends finished, with score coins plus reputation. A season that ends is removed from its slot, and its result goes into the records.
- Enter on the Evening goes to the Upgrades when the season goes on, and to the Season over screen when it has ended.

- The upgrades, each bought once (price; effect): Second till 80, a second till; Cool box 40, no extra spoilage on heat days; Sign 30, visitors look at the back row even with an empty basket; Extra crates 50, up to 12 crates; Awning 35, the rain's W is 80. The Upgrades' rows are Next day, then the five in that order. Enter on one not owned buys it when the coins are enough; with too few coins it changes nothing and the screen shows "Not enough coins" until the next word is given; on one owned it changes nothing. Enter on Next day starts the next day's Morning.
Stamps and records

- Stamps, in this order, are earned once and kept for good, across seasons and games: First coin (a visitor paid this day); Sold out (a good that had a crate on the stall and at least 1 unit in stock when the day opened had 0 units in stock when the day was over, before the order); Full stall (the day opened with 8 crates or more on the stall); Rain trade (taken 100 or more on a rain day); Good name (reputation 80 or more after the order is settled); Whole season (this is the season's last day and the coins after rent are 0 or more).
- The records keep the 5 best ended seasons: highest score first, and between equal scores the one that ended first; each with its score, the days played, its difficulty and whether it went bankrupt.
Screens

- Title: "Day Market", and a menu: New season, Continue (only while a slot holds a season), Records, Stamps, Settings, Quit. Quit ends the program (in a headless run it ends the run there, the state printed as it stood).

- Slots: the heading "New season" (from New season) or "Continue" (from Continue), then a row for each of the 3 slots: "Slot 1: Day 3 of 7, 52 coins" (the day, the season's length and the coins as saved) or "Slot 1: Empty". From New season, Enter starts a new season in the chosen slot, replacing whatever it held. From Continue, Enter on a slot holding a season starts that season's saved day's Morning again (its draws are the same as before); on an empty slot it changes nothing. Escape goes back to the title.

- Morning: "Morning", "Day 1 of 7", "Weather: Sun" (or Cloud, Rain, Heat), "Coins: 50", the rows "To the stall" and one per good as "Apples: 3 a unit, stock 12" (the day's wholesale price; the units in stock), the order as "Order: 6 Fish for 126" ("Order taken: 6 Fish for 126" once taken; no line when there is none), and "Not enough coins" when it applies.
- Stall: "Stall", "Day 1 of 7", the grid with its crates and the cursor, "Good: Apples", "Price: 4", "Stock: 12" (the selected good's price and units in stock), "Crates: 3 of 8" and "Enter: open".

- Day: the stall with its crates, the aisle with its visitors at their cells (the four types told apart), the queue and the tills, and "Day 1 of 7", "Weather: Sun", the time as "08:00" (08:00 plus the clock), "Speed: Slow" (or Hold, Fast, Rush), "Coins: 50", "Taken: 0", "Served: 0", "Walked out: 0", "Reputation: 50".

- Paused (Escape on the Morning, the Stall or the Day): "Paused" and a menu: Resume, Title. Resume, or Escape, goes back to the screen it came from, as it was; while paused the clock stands. Title gives the day up: the season stays in its slot as it was saved that Morning (anything bought since is not in it), and the screen is the title.

- Evening: "Evening", "Day 1 of 7", "Taken: 85", "Served: 12", "Walked out: 2", "Passed: 30", a line per good in catalogue order as "Apples: sold 8, spoiled 2, left 4" (units sold to visitors this day, units spoiled this evening, units in stock now), "Order delivered: 126" or "Order failed" (only when an order was taken), "Rent: 36", "Coins: 120", "Reputation: 61", "Tomorrow: Rain" (only when the season goes on), a line "Stamp: First coin" for each stamp earned this evening (in stamp order), and "Bankrupt" or "Season over" when the season ended this evening.
- Upgrades: "Upgrades", "Coins: 120", the rows "Next day" and one per upgrade as "Second till: 80" ("Second till: owned" once bought), and "Not enough coins" when it applies.
- Season over: "Season over" (or "Bankrupt"), "Score: 214", "Days: 7" (the days played), "Best: 300" (the best score in the records), "Enter: title". Enter goes to the title.

- Records: "Records", then a line per record, best first, as "Score 214, 7 days, Normal" (with ", bankrupt" at the end for one that went bankrupt: "Score 0, 2 days, Hard, bankrupt"), or "No records yet" when there are none. Enter or Escape goes to the title.
- Stamps: "Stamps", then a line per stamp in stamp order as "First coin: yes" or "First coin: no". Enter or Escape goes to the title.

- Settings: "Settings" and a menu: Language (English, Spanish; English at first), Difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard; Normal at first), Season (7 days, 3 days; 7 days at first), Back; shown as "Language: English", "Difficulty: Normal", "Season: 7 days", "Back". Left / Right change the chosen one and stop at either end. Enter on Back, or Escape, goes to the title.

- Menus and rows: each time a screen opens, its first entry is chosen; Up / Down move and stop at the first and last entry. A word that means nothing on the screen it comes on changes nothing (for example Escape on the Evening, Left on the title, put on the Morning, a speed word or finish anywhere but the Day).

- Every word the game shows is in English and in Spanish, from tables of strings, not written into the code; changing the language changes every word on screen at once. The game's name is the same in both. The examples in this brief are the English.
- The settings, the 3 slots, the stamps and the records are kept: a game started again later comes up with them. A fresh game has the default settings, three empty slots, no stamps and no records.
- It advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second; what happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn, and the same seed and inputs from the same kept things always give the same run.
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer two things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a seed, a number of ticks, where everything kept is kept (the settings, the slots, the stamps, the records), and a script of inputs (at tick T: one of up, down, left, right, enter, escape, next_good, prev_good, put, take, price_up, price_down, accept, hold, slow, fast, rush, finish, none; each acts once, after T ticks have run and before the next tick runs, even when the same word was given at the tick before; several words at the same tick act one after another in the order given; a word at tick 0 acts before anything runs), it starts at the title screen, runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick" (the ticks run so far in this headless run: N after N ticks, whatever screen it is on), "screen" (title, slots, settings, records, stamps, morning, stall, day, paused, evening, upgrades, season_over), "menu_index" (the chosen entry or row; 0 on a screen with none), "language" (en, es), "difficulty" (the setting: easy, normal, hard), "length" (the setting: 7 or 3), "texts" (every string on screen now, in order), "slots" (three entries, slot 1 first, each null or {"day", "coins", "length", "difficulty"} as saved), "slot" (1 to 3 while a season is being played, from New season or Continue until the Season over screen opens or the day is given up; null otherwise), "day", "season_difficulty", "season_length", "coins", "reputation", "weather" (sun, cloud, rain, heat: the day's), "forecast" (the season's weather, day 1 first), "upgrades" (those owned, in the brief's order, as second_till, cool_box, sign, extra_crates, awning), "crate_limit" (8 or 12), "wholesale" ({good: the day's wholesale price}), "order" (null, or {"good", "units", "pay", "taken"}), "stock" ({good: [{"units", "days_left"}]} with every good as a key, its batches with the fewest days left first, honey's days_left null), "prices" ({good: price}), "stall" ([{"x", "y", "good"}] ordered by x, then y), "cursor" ({"x", "y"}), "selected" (a good), "clock" (the day's clock in the Day and its pause, 480 on the Evening and the Upgrades, 0 everywhere else), "speed" (hold, slow, fast, rush in the Day and its pause; null elsewhere), "visitors" ([{"id", "minute", "type", "wants"}]: the day's visitor list, from the day's opening until the next Morning; [] otherwise), "aisle" ([{"id", "type", "x", "basket": [{"good", "units", "price"}], "budget_left"}] by number), "queue" ([{"id", "type", "joined", "basket"}] front first), "tills" ([{"visitor" (a number or null), "ends" (a minute or null)}], till 1 first, in the Day and its pause; [] elsewhere), "taken", "served", "walked_out", "passed", "spoiled" (the day's, cleared when a Morning starts), "sales" ([{"minute", "visitor", "goods": [{"good", "units", "price"}], "paid"}]: the day's payments, in order), "stamps" (those earned, in stamp order, as first_coin, sold_out, full_stall, rain_trade, good_name, whole_season), "records" ([{"score", "days", "difficulty", "bankrupt"}] best first)}. Goods are named apples, bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey; visitor types cook, tourist, bargain, regular. When no season is being played: day 0, coins 0, reputation 0, season_difficulty, season_length, weather and order null, forecast, upgrades, stall, visitors, aisle, queue, tills and sales [], wholesale, stock and prices {}, crate_limit 8, cursor (0, 0), selected apples, and taken, served, walked_out, passed and spoiled 0.
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 800 pixels wide and 480 tall.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The game, ready to run.

- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the headless run and the frame, where everything kept is kept, how to change a good, a visitor type, an upgrade or a stamp, how to add a language, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, starts at the title screen and prints the state as the brief's JSON object, with every key the brief names.
The frame is written as an 800 x 480 PNG after a headless run.

With nothing kept, the title's texts are Day Market, New season, Records, Stamps, Settings and Quit (no Continue), menu_index is 0, Up / Down stop at the first and last entry, and Quit ends the run with the state printed.

In Settings, Left / Right change the language between English and Spanish, the difficulty among Easy, Normal and Hard and the season between 7 days and 3 days, never past either end, starting at English, Normal and 7 days with the texts "Language: English", "Difficulty: Normal" and "Season: 7 days"; Escape, and Enter on Back, go to the title.

Language, difficulty and season length set in one headless run are the values a second run starts with (same place kept), and a fresh place starts with the defaults, three empty slots, no stamps and no records.

In Spanish every string in texts on every screen (title, slots, settings, records, stamps, morning, stall, day, paused, evening, upgrades, season over) is in Spanish, none left in English and none missing, the game's name apart, and choosing Spanish changes the settings screen's own texts at once.
The strings are in tables apart from the code, one per language, and README.md says how to add a language.
On a fresh place New season shows the heading "New season" and the rows "Slot 1: Empty", "Slot 2: Empty" and "Slot 3: Empty", and Escape goes back to the title.

Enter on a slot from New season starts a season there: screen morning, day 1, slot that number, coins 50, reputation 50, every good's stock empty, prices apples 4, bread 6, cheese 11, fish 14, flowers 7, honey 9, no upgrades, crate_limit 8, order null, and texts including "Morning", "Day 1 of 7" and "Coins: 50".

A season started at Easy has 60 coins and one started at Hard 40; one started at 3 days says "Day 1 of 3" and has a forecast of 3 entries; season_difficulty and season_length stay as they were when the settings are changed afterwards.
The forecast has one entry per day of the season, each sun, cloud, rain or heat; weather is the entry for the current day and the "Weather:" text follows it; the same seed gives the same forecast.

Each wholesale price is the good's base plus -1 to +2 (apples 1 to 4, bread 2 to 5, cheese 5 to 8, fish 6 to 9, flowers 2 to 5, honey 4 to 7), and each good's Morning row reads like "Apples: 3 a unit, stock 0" with that price and its stock.

Enter on a good's row buys 6 units: the coins go down by 6 times its wholesale price, its stock gains a batch of 6 units with the good's life as days_left (null for honey), a second lot of it that Morning makes that batch 12 units, and the row's stock follows.

With too few coins for a lot, Enter on the row changes neither coins nor stock and adds "Not enough coins" to the texts until the next word; a lot that would take a good's stock past 99 units changes nothing.

Day 1 has no order; from day 2 the order is a good with 4, 6 or 8 units and a pay of units times reference price times 3 / 2 rounded down, shown like "Order: 6 Fish for 126"; accept makes taken true and the line "Order taken: ...", and a second accept changes nothing.

When a Morning starts the season is saved: a later headless run on the same place shows that slot's row as "Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins" (for a new Normal season) and Continue on the title between New season and Records.

From Continue, Enter on a slot holding a season opens its Morning with the day, coins, reputation, stock, stall, prices, upgrades, forecast, wholesale prices and order it was saved with, whatever seed the game was started with now; Enter on an empty slot changes nothing.

Escape on the Morning, the Stall or the Day opens Paused (texts Paused, Resume, Title; the clock stands); Resume and Escape go back to the same screen and state; Title goes to the title and leaves the slot as saved that Morning, so a lot bought that Morning is not in it.

The Stall opens with the cursor at (0, 0) and apples selected, and its texts include "Stall", "Good: Apples", "Price: 4", "Stock: N" with the units of apples in stock, and "Crates: 0 of 8" on a new season.
In the Stall the cursor moves one cell for each of Up, Down, Left and Right (Up raises y) and stops at x 0 and 5 and at y 0 and 1.
next_good cycles the selection apples, bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey, apples, prev_good goes the other way, and the Good, Price and Stock texts follow the selection.

put places a crate of the selected good on the cursor's empty cell (stall gains its x, y and good, and "Crates: N of 8" follows), changes nothing on an occupied cell or with 8 crates placed, and take removes the cursor's crate and changes nothing on an empty cell.
price_up and price_down change the selected good's price by 1 and stop at 1 and at 3 times its reference price (12 for apples), and the Price text follows.
The stall and the prices stay as they were left into the next day, and through a save and Continue in a later headless run.
Enter on the Stall opens the day: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, the texts "08:00" and "Speed: Slow", taken, served, walked_out and passed 0, and the day's visitor list in visitors.

The visitor list has ids 1, 2, 3 in order, minutes strictly increasing within 0 to 479, types among cook, tourist, bargain and regular, and wants of distinct goods numbering 2, 1, 2 and 3 for those types; the same season seed and day give the same list, and another seed another.

At speed slow the clock goes up by 1 every 20 ticks, at fast every 5, at rush every tick, and at hold not at all while tick goes on and the screen stays day; a change of speed keeps the part of a minute already gone; the time and Speed texts follow.
finish ends the day before the next tick (screen evening, clock 480) with the same taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, coins and reputation as the same day run to its end at rush.
A day's result is the same at slow, at fast, at rush and with changes of speed and a hold in the middle: same season, same day, same coins, taken, served, walked_out, passed and sales.
A visitor arriving at minute m is on the aisle from clock m with x equal to the clock minus m, and is off the aisle from clock m + 6 (in the queue with joined m + 6, at a till, or gone).

A visitor with an empty basket takes only from front-row crates, one whose basket holds something also from the back-row crate of its column, and none takes a good that is not on its wants or is already in its basket.

With apples priced 4 in a front crate in column c and enough apples available, a cook wanting apples who arrives at minute m holds 2 apples at price 4 from clock m + c and its budget_left is 8 lower; at price 5 a cook takes none, while a tourist wanting apples takes one at price 6 and none at 7.
No visitor takes a good when its units times the price exceed its budget_left, and the units of a good held in all baskets together (aisle, queue and tills) never exceed that good's stock.
A visitor leaving the aisle with an empty basket is gone and passed goes up by 1, and one with goods joins the end of the queue with joined equal to its arrival minute plus 6.

A service that starts at minute s ends at s + 2 + the number of goods in the basket (tills shows it in ends); then coins and taken go up by the basket's total (less a tenth rounded down for a bargain visitor), its units leave stock from the batch with the fewest days_left, served and reputation go up by 1, and sales gains an entry with what was paid.

The order inside a minute holds: a till whose service ends at minute m takes the front of the queue in that same minute, and a visitor who leaves the aisle at minute m with the queue empty and a till free is at that till from minute m.

No queued visitor's wait (clock minus joined) is ever at or above its type's patience (cook 15, tourist 6, bargain 20, regular 10), and when one leaves the queue its goods are available again, reputation goes down by 2 and walked_out goes up by 1.
When the clock reaches 480 the screen is evening, and the visitors still on the aisle, in the queue or at a till are gone without paying and without adding to walked_out or passed.
With Second till bought, tills has two entries in the day and two visitors can be served at the same time, till 1 taking the front of the queue first.
With Sign bought, a visitor with an empty basket also takes from the back-row crate of its column.

A taken order whose units are in stock at the evening is delivered (coins up by its pay, the units gone, "Order delivered: N"), one whose units are not fails (reputation down by 5, "Order failed"), and an order not taken changes nothing.

At the evening every batch's days_left goes down by 1 and a batch at 0 is thrown away and counted in spoiled and in the good's "spoiled" line: bread bought that Morning is spoiled that evening, fish bought on a day is spoiled on the next day's evening, and honey never spoils.
On a heat day the batches lose 2 days at the evening without Cool box, and 1 day with it.
Rent at the evening is 20 at Normal, 15 at Easy and 30 at Hard plus 2 for each crate on the stall, shown as "Rent: N" and taken from the coins.

The Evening's texts include "Evening", the day, Taken, Served, Walked out and Passed matching the state, a line per good like "Apples: sold N, spoiled N, left N" matching the sales and stock, Rent, Coins, Reputation, and "Tomorrow: W" with the next day's forecast while the season goes on.

Enter on the Evening of a season that goes on shows Upgrades with "Upgrades", "Coins: N" and the rows Next day, "Second till: 80", "Cool box: 40", "Sign: 30", "Extra crates: 50", "Awning: 35", and Enter on Next day starts the next day's Morning with day one higher.

Buying an upgrade takes its price from the coins, puts it in upgrades and makes its row read like "Sign: owned"; buying it again changes nothing; with too few coins nothing changes and "Not enough coins" shows; Extra crates makes crate_limit 12 and "Crates: N of 12".

When the coins after rent are below 0 the season ends bankrupt: the Evening says "Bankrupt", the slot is empty, Enter shows Season over with "Bankrupt" and "Score: 0", and the records gain it with bankrupt true.

A season whose last day's evening leaves coins of 0 or more ends finished: Enter shows Season over with "Season over", "Score: N" equal to coins plus reputation, "Days: N" and "Best: N", its slot is emptied, and Continue is gone from the title when no other slot holds a season.

The records hold at most 5 ended seasons, highest score first and the earlier first between equal scores, shown like "Score 214, 7 days, Normal" (ending ", bankrupt" for a bankrupt one) or "No records yet", and a later headless run on the same place shows them too.

A stamp earned at an evening shows on it as a line like "Stamp: First coin" only the first time it is earned, is in stamps in stamp order, and the Stamps screen reads "First coin: yes" for it and "...: no" for the rest, also in a later headless run on the same place.
First coin is earned by a day in which a visitor paid, Full stall by a day opened with 8 crates or more, and Whole season by a 3-day season ended on its last day without going bankrupt.
Sold out is earned when a good with a crate on the stall and stock when the day opened has no stock left when the day is over, and not by a good that has no crate on the stall.
A day played after Continue in a later headless run gives the same visitors, sales and evening as the same day played with the same inputs in the unbroken game.

Two headless runs with the same seed, ticks and script, each starting from its own identical copy of what is kept, print identical states, and another seed gives another forecast, other wholesale prices or another visitor list.
A word that means nothing on its screen changes nothing: for example Escape on the Evening, Left on the title, put on the Morning, accept on the Stall, and finish or rush outside the Day.

The goods, the visitor types, the hourly rates and weather numbers, the upgrades and the stamps are data apart from the code, and README.md says how to change a good, a visitor type, an upgrade or a stamp.
The frame on the Stall shows the grid, the crates with the six goods told apart, the cursor, the selected good, its price and the crate count, where the state says they are.

The frame in a day shows the stall and its crates, the visitors on the aisle at their cells with the four types told apart, the queue and the tills, and the time, speed, coins, taken, served and reputation.
The frames of the title, slots, settings, morning, upgrades, paused, evening and season over screens show their texts, with the chosen entry or row marked where there is one.
README.md says how to play, where everything kept is kept, and gives commands for the two checks that work as written.
